findings.finding: Rarest-word picking undefined: MLT is tf*idf with min/max df; rarity alone picks typos/hashes; short texts keep common words; the source counts itself.
findings.answer: Decision 1: tf*idf with BM25 idf, max 25, min tf 1, drop df=0, drop df>max(10,N/10), drop digit and 12+ hex lexemes, summed-df budget 3,000, source/exclude_issue items subtracted from df, ties by df then lexeme; picker unit tests in task 11.

specDepartures.spec: Duplicate recall: copy the titles and specs of INFRA's issues closed as duplicates and of the issues they name, and report top-three hits for the 40-word OR query and the new keyword search.
specDepartures.plan: Also load every other INFRA issue's title and spec as competitors with production timestamps, use the duplicate's version-1 spec and the survivor's spec as of the duplicate's filing, load every issue open, and leave out (and count) pairs whose survivor is in another project or was filed later.
specDepartures.evidence: With only the pairs loaded both queries find nearly every survivor, and a tie fails 'lists the survivor for more of them'; the dispatch-first skill tells closers to copy the duplicate's unique content into the survivor, so a later survivor spec can hold the duplicate's text; a project-scoped check can never find a survivor in another project (gap analysis finding 12).
